core.title: List only declared wagons in a train
core.given: A non-excluded plan artifact contains a train whose wagon list names wagons (changed or not).
core.when: The plan is authored, edited or checked — a train's wagon list is written, a wagon declaration is renamed or removed, or existing plans are validated.
core.then: Every wagon the train's wagon list names is declared as a wagon declaration with a matching wagon URN.
prefer: Declare the missing wagon as a wagon declaration.
Or remove the wagon from the train.
When renaming or removing a wagon declaration, update every train that lists it in the same change.
avoid: Listing a wagon in a train that has no wagon declaration — a train ordering a wagon that does not exist cannot run.
Declaring an empty placeholder wagon solely to silence the check instead of planning the wagon or removing it from the train.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned (the stack-wide exclusion list, profile: roots.excluded).
core.why: A train ordering a wagon that does not exist cannot run. Wagon membership is the train-specific case of reference resolution.
evidence: The stack's plan-integrity check reports no unresolved train wagon across all non-excluded plans.
For each wagon named in each train's wagon list, a reviewer finds a matching wagon declaration.
The rule has a failing fixture (a train listing an undeclared wagon) that the check rejects.
verification: Check: every entry in a scanned train's wagon list must match a declared wagon URN; any unmatched entry is a finding.
Scan scope: applies to every scanned train, not only changed ones; pre-existing unresolved wagon references are findings regardless of what the current edit touched.
Never scan the stack-wide excluded vendored and generated trees (profile: roots.excluded); the exact classification of what is vendored or generated is owned by the stack's checker.

Enforced by the stack's plan-integrity check, held to the same per-rule checks as every convention: a statement, strict disposition, a failing fixture, relationship edges. The concrete detector, validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details.

values: plan integrity check: unresolved train wagon
train wagon list added or edited

fires: Checking any non-excluded plan, including an unchanged one, whose train's wagon list already names a wagon with no matching wagon declaration.
A planner edits only a wagon's content in a plan where some train already lists an undeclared wagon — the pre-existing unresolved reference is still a finding.
A planner adds a wagon reference to a train's wagon list without a matching wagon declaration in the plan.
A planner renames or deletes a wagon declaration while a train still lists the old reference.
A train lists a wagon reference with a typo that matches no declared wagon.
doesNotFire: Every wagon named in every non-excluded train's wagon list has a matching wagon declaration.
Plan-like artifacts inside the stack's never-scanned vendored and generated trees (profile: roots.excluded).
Edits to a wagon's content that keep its wagon declaration, provided every train wagon reference in the scanned plans resolves to a declared wagon (pre-existing unresolved references still fire).

neutralityNotes: 'Train' and 'wagon' are treated as stack-neutral planning vocabulary (both are artifact kinds in the closed urn group); only their concrete syntax is profile-driven: the `wagons:` list via the proposed idiom.plan_syntax#train_wagon_list and the `wagon:<slug>` declaration via urn.wagon. The exact excluded trees exist only as the roots.excluded profile value; the checker keeps ownership of classifying them. Validator/finding ids and the package-guard-vs-canonical-planner-node enforcement split stay Bun-only: which component owns the plan-integrity check is a realization choice, so the core requires the check without restricting its owner. The alias and audit metadata stay Bun-only. Severity '3' is kept as declared because severity and disposition belong to the rule, though the numeric scale itself is a convention of this package family.
